gate_rule: 2-of-3: CALL when >=2 instruments clear 0.95 the same way and none contradicts by >0.20 the other way; p_gate = median

instruments.market_source: Polymarket (gamma-api events which-party-will-win-the-house/senate-in-2026), fetched 2026-11-02 ~07:30 UTC; house_dem 0.915 -> 0.945 (bid .94/ask .95), senate_dem 0.645 -> 0.725 (bid .72/ask .73) since 10-26
instruments.model_note: Silver Bulletin average D 51.2 / R 42.5 = D+8.7 as reported by Newsweek ~2026-11-01 (prior D+9.1 on 10-23); RCP 10/8-10/29 D+8.4, PollCheck (11-01) D+8.2 consistent

quality_flags: Resolves in 10 days - the fastest real-world test the world engine will get.
Senate model is the race-level correlated Monte Carlo roll-up (USMIDRACES2026, scripts/usmid_races.py): 35 structural per-seat probits with one shared national error term. Candidate-blind by design.
Model tipping-point (+2.5) is taken from published redistricting analyses, not fitted by us.

rules: House majority = party holding >= 218 of 435 seats per final certified results, NOT election-night leads; uncalled races resolve by their eventual certified winner
Senate majority = party controlling the floor at seating, with independents counted toward the party they caucus with (caucusing rule); a 50-50 Senate resolves to the Vice President's party
Rows resolve early, before 2027-01-03, if and when AP-called races put control beyond arithmetic dispute
A seat vacant at seating (death/resignation after certification) counts for the party that won it
Recounts and litigation: resolution waits for certified outcomes; no row resolves on a contested margin
resolution.source: Official state certifications as aggregated by Associated Press race calls; control counted at the seating of the 120th Congress (2027-01-03)
